Conversation field guide · 2 July–10 August 2026

Three useful things to notice

The supplied records from 40 sessions support three recurring error patterns: marking finished past events, ordering embedded questions, and counting uncountable nouns.

Choose a focus below. Each includes a source example and an optional quick application. These are priorities to notice—not a measure of your overall accuracy.

You can switch focuses or stop here. No practice is required.

How the evidence was chosen

Each selected pattern appears in at least three distinct supplied sessions. The navigation counts sessions with a supporting error record, not all occasions when you used that structure.

There are 10 supporting records for past events, 7 for embedded questions, and 8 for uncountable nouns—one per supporting session within each focus. Identical examples from different sessions are grouped in the source lists. Unchanged records do not provide a full denominator for calculating an error rate.

Not every proposed change is a necessary correction:

  • The eight “very like” records all come from one session (M21-U03–M21-U10), so they do not establish a recurring pattern across sessions.
  • “I think the plan is pretty good” and “The person who I spoke to was friendly” are acceptable conversational English (M06-U03; M30-U04).
  • “Because I was tired” is an acceptable answer to the recorded question “Why did you stop?” (M12-U04).
  • “I have a little time this evening” matches the intended meaning of some available time (M18-U03). “I am looking forward to seeing you” is already correct (M24-U04).

Source pairs below reproduce the supplied wording. Applications are newly written teaching examples, not additional evidence.
